info.timeAllocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
info.description: The course covers the basic knowledge neccessary for transmitting and receiving information using today's communication technologies. It is the introduction to communication systems: analogue vs. digital communications, analogue modulation techniques (amplitude modulation, frequency modulation, phase modulation), broadcast radio and TV systems, source coding, communication channels (noise, bandwidth), signalling over bandlimited channels (matched filter, intersymbol interference (ISI), Nyquist criterion), binary digital modulation techniques (amplitude shift keying, frequency shift keying, phase shift keying). Topics covered: Introduction; Fourier Representation of Signals and Systems; Amplitude Modulation; Angle Modulation; Pulse Modulation: Transition from Analog to Digital Communications; Baseband Data Transmission; Digital Band-Pass Modulation Techniques; Random Signals and Noise; Noise in Analog Communications; Noise in Digital Communications; System and Noise Calculations

materials.author: B. P. Lathi, Zhi Ding

clos.loDetails: Understand and explain the fundamental concepts of communication systems, including analog and digital communications, as well as the structure and functions of basic system blocks.
Analyze signals and systems in both the time and frequency domains, and apply Fourier analysis to characterize communication signals.
Analyze and evaluate analog and digital modulation and transmission techniques, including the effects of noise and bandwidth on system performance.
Apply fundamental principles of digital communications and information theory to analyze system performance and support the design of basic communication systems.

Apply practical communication engineering skills to analyze and solve basic communication system problems, and collaborate effectively in teams to discuss technical ideas, share responsibilities, and produce joint technical reports or presentations.

Demonstrate professional communication and social skills by presenting technical concepts clearly, engaging in constructive discussions, respecting diverse viewpoints, and adhering to ethical and professional standards in teamwork and academic activities.
